newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE euroyen ends up on position adjustment.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE euroyen ends up on position adjustment.

text.p: The key December three-month euroyen futures contract ended slightly higher on Friday.
Position adjustment after the previous day's sharp fall pushed the December up, but the market lacked momentum to go even higher, a trader for a brokerage house said.
Industrial output data released in the afternoon had little effect on the market, as it was mostly within the market's expectations, traders said.

The December was sold briefly after the Ministry of International Trade and Industry released a growth forecast of 1.0 percent in manufacturers' output for April, but such selling did not last, the brokerage house trader said.
Traders said the market will now be focusing on the Bank of Japan's key "tankan" corporate sentiment survey due on April 2.
MITI also said on Friday that Japan's industrial production in February fell a preliminary 3.4 percent from the previous month.
The fall in output in February was in line with expectations and had little effect on the market, traders said.
The Bank of Japan injected a net 700 billion yen into the money market, maintaining its accommodative stance.
The morning operation left the market with a fund surplus of about 90 billion yen.
Traders said the weighted average of the key overnight call rate was likely to be 0.51 percent, unchanged from Thursday.
"The rate has been rising in the afternoon so it is hard to say for sure, but 0.51 percent is likely to be the weighted average," a foreign bank trader said.
Relatively light trade in the key overnight call rate took place at 0.54 percent, a regional bank trader said.
But the traded amount is probably too small to push up the weighted average, the trader said.
Traders said they expect the BOJ to maintain an accommodative stance on Monday.
The BOJ may decide to increase the amount of surplus left in the market sometime next week if upward pressure on the key overnight call rate remains strong, traders said.
The key three-month certificates of deposit were tagged with a sell quote of 0.55 percent on Friday, down from a sell quote of 0.57 percent on Thursday, traders said.
